neighbours.label: the slot for the thing required after take / need / require / have to in a 'what it takes' frame, strongest when negated ('it doesn't take a genius', 'don't need any', 'don't have to be')
fire: Honestly, it doesn't take a rocket scientist to work out where the money went.
You don't need any special training to use the new software.
One doesn't have to be a lawyer to see that the contract is unfair.
It hardly takes a detective to notice the muddy footprints in the hall.
The trail is easy, so walkers don't need any climbing gear.
As the saying goes, it takes a village to raise a child.
You don't have to be rich to travel well in Portugal.
This simple soup doesn't require any fancy ingredients.
quiet: After dinner they decided to take a stroll around the harbour.
She wanted to have a word with the manager about the bill.
A great deal of work must be done before the school can reopen.
He asked whether there were any letters for him at the desk.
The walkers carried a map and a flask of tea.
My brother is a lawyer and his wife is a detective.
The children took a bus to the museum on Saturday.
Everything needs to be finished before the guests arrive.

notes: Card: 'doesn't take a', 'need any', 'have to be'; the + pole is the other side (must / needs to be done). Probing: 'doesn't take a genius' 1.06, 'don't have to be' 0.63, 'need any' 0.61, 'takes two people' 0.56; 'take a walk' 0.05, 'must be done' 0.11.
